#### Hypothesis 1: Smaller parties' seat-share gain {#sec-h1-results}

@fig-small-parties-relative compares smaller parties' combined seat shares under the observed Double Pukelsheim allocation and the counterfactual Hagenbach-Bischoff allocation for every cleaned election. Smaller parties are defined as parties with less than 10% of the vote share in the analyzed area. The x-axis reports their combined share of analyzed seats, while the y-axis reports their combined vote share. The grey line connects the two allocations derived from the same election, and each election is labelled at its Double Pukelsheim point. This seat-share difference is the outcome used to assess Hypothesis 1 and allows comparisons across elections with different numbers of analyzed seats. The corresponding comparison in absolute seat counts is provided in @fig-small-parties-absolute in Appendix 3.

```{r}
#| label: h1-data-and-plot-setup
#| include: false
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

# Restrict the tie check to parties below the 10% vote-share threshold.
small_party_rows <- all_elections |>
  filter(small_party == 1L)

# A slash marks alternative HB seat totals from an unresolved draw.
if (any(str_detect(small_party_rows$seats_hb, fixed("/")))) {
  stop("Resolve smaller-party HB ties before plotting.")
}

# Aggregate smaller parties within each election under both seat rules.
small_party_summary <- all_elections |>
  group_by(election_id) |>
  summarise(
    parliament_size = first(parliament_size),
    seats_allocated_dp = first(seats_allocated_dp),
    vote_share_small_parties = sum(vote_share[small_party == 1L]),
    # Only smaller-party seats enter the HB–DP comparison.
    seats_hb = sum(as.integer(seats_hb[small_party == 1L])),
    seats_dp = sum(seats_dp[small_party == 1L]),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    is_graubuenden = str_starts(election_id, "GR_"),
    # Express the DP gain as a share of seats included in the comparison.
    seat_gain_pp = 100 * (seats_dp - seats_hb) / seats_allocated_dp
  )

# Put both systems on separate rows for plotting and calculate seat shares.
small_party_plot_data <- small_party_summary |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(seats_hb, seats_dp),
    names_to = "system",
    values_to = "seats_small_parties"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    seat_share_small_parties = 100 * seats_small_parties / seats_allocated_dp,
    # Fix the legend order across both figures.
    system = factor(recode(system, seats_hb = "Hagenbach-Bischoff", seats_dp = "Double Pukelsheim"),
                    levels = c("Hagenbach-Bischoff", "Double Pukelsheim"))
  )

# Summarize election-level gains and the mean weighted by analyzed seats.
h1_stats <- small_party_summary |>
  filter(!is_graubuenden) |>
  summarise(
    elections = n(), mean_gain = mean(seat_gain_pp),
    weighted_mean_gain = weighted.mean(seat_gain_pp, seats_allocated_dp),
    q1 = quantile(seat_gain_pp, .25), median = median(seat_gain_pp),
    q3 = quantile(seat_gain_pp, .75),
    above_five = sum(seat_gain_pp > 5)
  )

# Draw either the seat-count or seat-share version of the same comparison.
small_party_plot <- function(x, x_title, label, percent = FALSE) {
  # Keep all endpoints in one repel layer
  label_data <- small_party_plot_data |>
    mutate(
      plot_label = if_else(system == "Double Pukelsheim", .data[[label]], ""),
      label_colour = if_else(is_graubuenden, "Context only", as.character(system))
    )
  # Repulsion needs obstacles along horizontal comparison lines
  line_obstacles <- small_party_plot_data |>
    group_by(election_id) |>
    reframe(
      !!x := seq(min(.data[[x]]), max(.data[[x]]), length.out = 25),
      vote_share_small_parties = first(vote_share_small_parties),
      plot_label = "", label_colour = "Context only"
    )
  ggplot(small_party_plot_data, aes(x = .data[[x]], y = vote_share_small_parties,
                                   color = system, shape = system)) +
    # Connect the two outcomes from each election
    geom_line(aes(group = election_id), color = "grey75", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_point(data = filter(small_party_plot_data, !is_graubuenden), size = 3.2) +
    geom_point(data = filter(small_party_plot_data, is_graubuenden),
           color = "grey60", shape = 16, size = 3.2) +
    # Solve all label positions together, white fills keep lines out of text.
    geom_label_repel(
      data = bind_rows(label_data, line_obstacles), inherit.aes = FALSE,
      aes(x = .data[[x]], y = vote_share_small_parties,
          label = plot_label, color = label_colour),
      fill = "white", label.size = 0, label.padding = 0.12,
      size = 3.2, show.legend = FALSE, max.overlaps = Inf,
      box.padding = 0.4, point.padding = 0.15, force = 3,
      max.time = Inf, max.iter = 30000,
      min.segment.length = 0, segment.color = "grey65",
      segment.size = 0.35, seed = 2026
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Hagenbach-Bischoff" = "#D55E00",
                                  "Double Pukelsheim" = "#0072B2",
                                  "Context only" = "grey60"),
                       breaks = c("Hagenbach-Bischoff", "Double Pukelsheim")) +
    # Format the x-axis as percentages only in the relative figure.
    scale_x_continuous(labels = if (percent) \(x) paste0(x, "%") else waiver(),
                       expand = expansion(mult = c(0.08, 0.12))) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.08, 0.12))) +
    labs(title = "Representation of Smaller Parties Across Elections",
         subtitle = "Observed Double Pukelsheim and counterfactual Hagenbach-Bischoff allocations",
         x = x_title, y = "Aggregated vote share of smaller parties (%)",
         color = "Electoral system", shape = "Electoral system") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(legend.position = "top", legend.title = element_text(size = 11),
          legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
          plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11), axis.title = element_text(size = 11),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
}
# Adding sensitivity check with 8% smaller-parties threshold
sensitivity_8 <- all_elections |> 
  filter(!str_starts(election_id, "GR_")) |>
  group_by(election_id) |>
  summarise(
    small_parties = sum(vote_share < 8),
    gain_pp = 100 * (
      sum(seats_dp[vote_share < 8]) -
      sum(as.integer(seats_hb[vote_share < 8]))
    ) / first(seats_allocated_dp)
  )
# second sensitivity check with 12% threshold
sensitivity_12 <- all_elections |> 
  filter(!str_starts(election_id, "GR_")) |>
  group_by(election_id) |>
  summarise(
    small_parties = sum(vote_share < 12),
    gain_pp = 100 * (
      sum(seats_dp[vote_share < 12]) -
      sum(as.integer(seats_hb[vote_share < 12]))
    ) / first(seats_allocated_dp)
  )

mean(sensitivity_8$gain_pp)
mean(sensitivity_12$gain_pp)

# Elections with parties below 8% but no aggregate seat gain under DP
no_gain_8 <- sensitivity_8 |>
  filter(small_parties > 0, gain_pp <= 0)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-small-parties-relative
#| fig-cap: "Smaller-party seat-share gain across all 31 elections" 
#| fig-width: 8.3
#| fig-height: 6.5
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

# Reuse the plot with seat shares and one election identifier per comparison.
small_party_plot("seat_share_small_parties", "Seats won by smaller parties (%)", "election_id", TRUE)
```

::: {.callout-note title="Hypothesis 1 summary"}
Across all `r h1_stats$elections` elections (Graubünden excluded), the unweighted mean gain in smaller parties' share of analyzed seats was `r sprintf("%.1f", h1_stats$mean_gain)` percentage points (Q1: `r sprintf("%.1f", h1_stats$q1)`; median: `r sprintf("%.1f", h1_stats$median)`; Q3: `r sprintf("%.1f", h1_stats$q3)`). The mean weighted by each election's number of analyzed seats was `r sprintf("%.1f", h1_stats$weighted_mean_gain)` percentage points. `r h1_stats$above_five` individual elections exceeded five percentage points.
:::

These results descriptively support Hypothesis 1 and indicate that smaller parties indeed in the 31 elections held receive a larger share of the analyzed seats under Double Pukelsheim than under Hagenbach-Bischoff. The effect is especially pointed out, through that in every election where small parties contested (every election but Uri 2020), they aggregately received a larger seat share. This finding is in accordance with Leuzinger's observation for the seven from him examined elections (Leuzinger, 2018, p.42). The weighted mean, unweighted mean and median are all relatively close to each other, indicating that the effect is not driven by a few elections with many seats and that the positive effect isn't determined by extreme outliers. 

The average gain differs across the cantons for e.g. is there the Canton of Schaffhausen, with a stable high seat gain for smaller parties. There the high seat-share gain can be partially explained through the decision to treat affiliated parties as independent lists. Therefore these affiliated lists were classified as smaller parties, if they didn't reach the 10% threshold themselfs and with that higher the relative gain for smaller parties. Across the five Schaffhausen elections, the average effect of this decision is that the relative gain drops from 15.67 to 8.67 percentage points. Taking the effect into account, the mechanical transition effect in Schaffhausen is still relatively big compared to other cantons. Cantons with constantly relatively low stable seat gain shares on the other hand are for e.g. Uri, Zug and Schwyz. 

The general finding is further robust to alternative definitions of smaller parties. Using a vote-share cutoff of less than 8%, the mean gain is `r sprintf("%.2f", mean(sensitivity_8$gain_pp))` percentage points. Also do the smaller parties c further smaller parties collectively receive a higher seat share under Double Pukelsheim in `r sum(sensitivity_8$gain_pp > 0)` of the `r sum(sensitivity_8$small_parties > 0)` where atleast one parliamentary party with a maximum of 8% vote-share contested. The exception is  `r paste(str_replace(no_gain_8$election_id, "_", " 20"), collapse = " and ")` , where the aggregated difference is zero and the upper-allocation process isn't done across the whole canton. With a cutoff of less than 12%, the mean gain is `r sprintf("%.2f", mean(sensitivity_12$gain_pp))` percentage points. Regarding the collectively higher seat share in this case, in  `r sum(sensitivity_12$gain_pp > 0)` of the `r sum(sensitivity_12$small_parties > 0)` relevant elections, the smaller parties received a higher seat-share gain. With again Uri 2020, being the exclusion, where no party with less than 12% vote-share ran.

As a further sensitivity and robustness measure, the results were tested with a leave one canton out check. In that check each canton is omitted once and then the weighted and unweighted mean gain are recalculated. The positive seat-share gain persisted across each check. Which fits the finding that in 30 of 31 elections, there was a positive aggregated seat-share gain for smaller parties. The detailed results for the checks can be found in the Appendix in @sec-leave-one-out. 

These measures deliver a profound picture over the aggregated seat-share gain of smaller parties, but they don't reveal which category of smaller parties profit most from the transition. Is it rather smaller parties between 3-4% or ones with 8-10%? Therefore this subanalysis examines this for all 31 transition elections. Both party-size figures additionally show observations from the two Graubünden elections for context. Since Graubünden previously used Majorz, its HB comparison is hypothetical and its results are only contextual. 

```{r}
#| label: fig-party-size-gains
#| fig-cap: "Mechanical seat-share gains by party vote-share group"
#| fig-width: 7.5
#| fig-height: 4.8
#| echo: false
#| message: false

library(tidyverse)

party_size_plot_data <- all_elections |>
  filter(
    vote_share >= 0,
    vote_share < 15 # Filter only parties with vote-shares below 15%
  ) |>
  mutate(
    comparison = if_else(str_starts(election_id, "GR_"),
                         "Graubünden (context)", "Transition cantons"),
    gain_pp = 100 * ( # Gain as percentage points of analyzed seats.
      seats_dp - as.integer(seats_hb)
    ) / seats_allocated_dp,

    size_group = cut( # Group parties by their election-specific vote share.
      vote_share,
      breaks = c(0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 15), # Eight boundaries define seven groups.
      labels = c(
        "0-<2%", "2-<4%", "4-<6%",
        "6-<8%", "8-<10%", "10-<12%", "12-<15%"
      ),
      right = FALSE # Include lower boundaries: 4% enters 4-<6%.
    )
  )

# Keep the transition sample separate for all summaries and counts.
party_size_data <- party_size_plot_data |>
  filter(comparison == "Transition cantons")

party_size_means <- party_size_data |>
  group_by(size_group) |>
  summarise(mean_gain_pp = mean(gain_pp), n = n(), .groups = "drop") # Equal weight per party-election.

ggplot(party_size_data, aes(x = size_group, y = gain_pp)) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    colour = "grey50",
    linewidth = 0.4
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = party_size_plot_data,
    aes(colour = comparison, shape = comparison),
    position = position_jitter(
      width = 0.12, height = 0, seed = 2026 # Separate dots horizontally only.
    ),
    alpha = 0.6,
    size = 2
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = party_size_means,
    aes(y = mean_gain_pp), # Mark each group's mean.
    colour = "#000000",
    shape = 18,
    size = 4
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = party_size_means,
    aes(y = mean_gain_pp, label = sprintf("%.2f", mean_gain_pp)), # Label means in pp.
    nudge_x = 0.18,
    hjust = 0,
    colour = "#000000",
    size = 3
  ) +
  scale_x_discrete(
    labels = setNames(
      paste0(
        party_size_means$size_group,
        "\n(n = ", party_size_means$n, ")"
      ),
      party_size_means$size_group
    )
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = c("Transition cantons" = "#0072B2", "Graubünden (context)" = "#707070"),
    breaks = c("Transition cantons", "Graubünden (context)"), name = NULL
  ) +
  scale_shape_manual(
    values = c("Transition cantons" = 16, "Graubünden (context)" = 1),
    breaks = c("Transition cantons", "Graubünden (context)"), name = NULL
  ) +
  labs(
    x = "Party vote-share group in the analyzed area",
    y = "Seat-share gain under DP relative to HB (pp)",
    caption = paste(
      "Black diamonds and labels: transition-canton group means (pp).",
      "n counts transition observations only.\n",
      "Grey open circles: Graubünden's hypothetical HB comparison (context only)."
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0)
  )


```

The summary of the `r nrow(party_size_data)` party-election observations shows that parties between 4-6% vote share tend to profit the most from the implementation of the Double Pukelsheim. For parties with more than 10% the seat-share gain is on average markedly lower. For parties with atleast 12 and below 15% the average gain reaches a point, where the parties with 0.46 percentage points barely profit anymore from the implementation. On the other side of the scale for the parties below 2% one can see that they profit slightly, while there are multiple observations were a list didn't profit at all. From the 66 observations below 2%, 45 lists receive no seats under eiter allocation. This partly explains the limited gains for parties in that group. Overall does the analysis, show that smaller parties tend to profit from the implementation whereas bigger parties in average subsequently lose their prior advantage under the old system. To be able to identify a possible gradual pattern, the analysis was also done without grouping. The figure there shows no clear monotonic relationship, further can the substantial variation between parties of the same vote share be seen throughout the analysis. With the observation, that observations at a very low share cluster around zeero, while positive gains occur across most of the remaining range. Further do most negative observations appear in the upper end of the range. The figure can be found in the Appendix in @sec-additional-analysis.

To sum up the analysis of Hypothesis 1: It covers all 31 cantonal parliamentary elections held under Double Pukelsheim in Switzerland from the cantons that transitioned from Hagenbach-Bischoff. Across these elections, smaller parties received under all definitions of smaller parties, a higher aggregate seat share under Double Pukelsheim. This pattern also persisted throghout almost every within election comparison of smaller parties. Further did the analyis show, that parties between 4% and below 10% profited most from the implementation of the Double Pukelsheim. These findings are based on the mechanical allocation difference conditional on the observed votes and specified counterfactual rules and therefore do not capture the whole transition effect. The next section examines whether the magnitude of this effect is associated with the cantons district magnitudes. 

#### Exploratory question 1: Differences by district magnitude

This section examines how district magnitude varies across the cantons included in the analysis, considering both typical district size and variation within cantons. @tbl-district-magnitude summarizes these differences using district counts, the share of districts with fewer than nine seats, mean and median district magnitudes aswell as the coefficient of variation. All measures refer to the fixed historical baseline defined in @sec-measures , with Schaffhausen adjusted to 60 seats. Graubünden is shown for context only.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-district-magnitude
#| tbl-cap: "Pre-reform district structure by canton"
#| tbl-colwidths: [13, 14, 14, 14, 15, 14, 14]
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

eq1_env <- new.env(parent = globalenv()) 

sys.source(here("data_cleaning_cantons", "00_functions.R"), eq1_env) # Load the shared cleaning functions 
eq1_env$district_registry <- list() # create empty list to store the values
eq1_env$original_finalize <- eq1_env$finalize_election_data # Keep the original function before wrapping it.
eq1_env$finalize_election_data <- function(
    hb_results, dp_results, canton, year, parliament_size = NULL) {
  caller <- parent.frame() # Access the reader that called this function and its local district table.
  table_name <- switch(canton, AG = "districts", GR = "hb_by_district",
                       SH = "district_totals", ZH = "district_seats",
                       "district_results") 
  district_name <- if (canton == "AG") "location_name" else "district" # Standardize Aargau's name column.
  districts <- get(table_name, envir = caller, inherits = FALSE) |> 
    transmute(district = .data[[district_name]], district_seats) |> # Keep only district names and seat counts
    distinct() # Remove repeated identical rows.
  stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(districts$district), !anyNA(districts),
            all(districts$district_seats > 0),
            all(districts$district_seats == floor(districts$district_seats))) # Stop if names or seat counts are invalid.
  result <- original_finalize(hb_results, dp_results, canton, year, parliament_size) # Calculate the usual election output
  stopifnot(sum(districts$district_seats) == first(result$seats_allocated_dp)) # District seats must match DP seat coverage.
  id <- first(result$election_id) # Election identifier
  district_registry[[id]] <<- districts |>
    mutate(election_id = id, canton = canton, year = year, .before = 1) 
  result # Return the original election output 
}
environment(eq1_env$finalize_election_data) <- eq1_env 

eq1_codes <- c("AG", "GR", "NW", "SH", "SZ", "UR", "VS", "ZG", "ZH") # Cantons included, with GR for context.
for (code in eq1_codes) { # Load each canton's reader into the separate workspace.
  expressions <- parse(here("data_cleaning_cantons", paste0("canton_", code, ".R")),
                       encoding = "UTF-8") 
  for (expression in expressions) {
    
    if (is.call(expression) && identical(expression[[1]], as.name("print"))) next
    eval(expression, envir = eq1_env) # Run the remaining definitions in the separate workspace.
  }
}
eq1_parties <- map_dfr(eq1_codes, function(code) {
  get(paste0("process_canton_", code), envir = eq1_env)() # Run each reader; map_dfr stacks the resulting rows.
})
eq1_districts <- bind_rows(eq1_env$district_registry) # Stack the captured district tables across elections.
stopifnot(n_distinct(eq1_parties$election_id) == 33L,
          n_distinct(eq1_districts$election_id) == 33L,
          isTRUE(all.equal(arrange(eq1_parties, election_id, parties),
                           arrange(all_elections, election_id, parties)))) 

# Use the same election-level outcome as H1; validate analyzed seat coverage.
eq1_elections <- eq1_districts |>
  group_by(canton, election_id, year) |> # Calculate coverage separately for each election.
  summarise(
    districts = n(), analyzed_seats = sum(district_seats), # Count districts and total their seats.
    .groups = "drop" # Return an ordinary, ungrouped table.
  ) |>
  left_join(small_party_summary |>
              select(election_id, seats_allocated_dp, seat_gain_pp),
            by = "election_id") # Match each election to H1's smaller-party gain
stopifnot(!anyNA(eq1_elections),
          all(eq1_elections$analyzed_seats == eq1_elections$seats_allocated_dp)) # Check complete matches and equal seat coverage.

# Fixed last-pre-reform allocations. Named vectors preserve district provenance.

eq1_baseline_seats <- list( 
  AG = c(Aarau = 16, Baden = 30, Bremgarten = 16, Brugg = 11, Kulm = 9,
         Laufenburg = 6, Lenzburg = 12, Muri = 7, Rheinfelden = 10,
         Zofingen = 15, Zurzach = 8),
  GR = c(Alvaschein = 2, Avers = 1, Belfort = 1, Berguen = 1, Bregaglia = 1,
         Brusio = 1, Calanca = 1, Chur = 20, Churwalden = 1, Davos = 6,
         Disentis = 4, Domleschg = 3, Fuenf_Doerfer = 12, Ilanz = 6,
         Jenaz = 1, Klosters = 3, Kueblis = 1, Lumnezia_Lugnez = 2,
         Luzein = 1, Maienfeld = 4, Mesocco = 2, Oberengadin = 8,
         Poschiavo = 2, Ramosch = 1, Rhaezuens = 7, Rheinwald = 1,
         Roveredo = 3, Ruis = 1, Safien = 1, Schams = 1, Schanfigg = 2,
         Schiers = 3, Seewis = 1, Suot_Tasna = 3, Sur_Tasna = 1,
         Surses = 1, Thusis = 4, Trins = 5, Val_Muestair = 1),
  NW = c(Stans = 11, Ennetmoos = 3, Dallenwil = 3, Stansstad = 6,
         Oberdorf = 5, Buochs = 8, Ennetbuergen = 6, Wolfenschiessen = 3,
         Beckenried = 5, Hergiswil = 8, Emmetten = 2),
  # Published adjustment of the 2004 district structure to a 60-seat parliament.
  SH = c(Schaffhausen = 28, Neuhausen = 8, Klettgau = 12, Reiat = 7,
         Stein = 4, Buchberg_Ruedlingen = 1),
  SZ = c(Schwyz = 10, Arth = 7, Ingenbohl = 6, Muothathal = 2, Steinen = 2,
         Sattel = 1, Rothenthurm = 1, Oberiberg = 1, Unteriberg = 1,
         Lauerz = 1, Steinerberg = 1, Morschach = 1, Alpthal = 1, Illgau = 1,
         Riemenstalden = 1, Gersau = 1, Lachen = 5, Altendorf = 4,
         Galgenen = 3, Vorderthal = 1, Innerthal = 1, Schuebelbach = 6,
         Tuggen = 2, Wangen = 3, Reichenburg = 2, Einsiedeln = 10,
         Kuessnacht = 8, Wollerau = 4, Freienbach = 10, Feusisberg = 3),
  UR = c(Altdorf = 15, Buerglen = 7, Erstfeld = 6, Schattdorf = 9), 
  VS = c(Goms = 2, Oestlich_Raron = 2, Brig = 12, Visp = 12,
         Westlich_Raron = 4, Leuk = 6, Siders = 17, Ering = 5, Sitten = 17,
         Gundis = 10, Martinach = 16, Entremont = 6, St_Maurice = 5,
         Monthey = 16),
  ZG = c(Zug = 19, Oberaegeri = 4, Unteraegeri = 6, Menzingen = 3,
         Baar = 15, Cham = 10, Huenenberg = 6, Steinhausen = 6, Risch = 6,
         Walchwil = 3, Neuheim = 2),
  ZH = c(Zuerich_1_2 = 5, Zuerich_3_9 = 13, Zuerich_4_5 = 5,
         Zuerich_6_10 = 9, Zuerich_7_8 = 7, Zuerich_11_12 = 11,
         Dietikon = 11, Affoltern = 6, Horgen = 16, Meilen = 13, Hinwil = 11,
         Uster = 16, Pfaeffikon = 7, Winterthur_Stadt = 13,
         Winterthur_Land = 7, Andelfingen = 4, Buelach = 16, Dielsdorf = 10)
)
eq1_baseline_years <- c(AG = 2005L, GR = 2018L, NW = 2010L, SH = 2004L,
                        SZ = 2012L, UR = 2016L, VS = 2013L, ZG = 2010L,
                        ZH = 2003L) # Historical reference years
eq1_baseline_totals <- c(AG = 140, GR = 120, NW = 60, SH = 60, SZ = 100,
                         UR = 37, VS = 130, ZG = 80, ZH = 180) # Expected seat totals
stopifnot(identical(names(eq1_baseline_seats), eq1_codes),
          all(map_lgl(eq1_baseline_seats, function(x) {
            !anyNA(x) && !anyDuplicated(names(x)) &&
              all(x > 0 & x == floor(x))
          })),
          all(map_dbl(eq1_baseline_seats, sum) == eq1_baseline_totals)) # Check canton order, valid district entries, and seat totals.
eq1_baseline <- imap_dfr(eq1_baseline_seats, function(seats, code) { # Process each vector and its canton name
  tibble(canton = code, reference_year = eq1_baseline_years[[code]], # Match the canton to its reference year.
         baseline_districts = length(seats), # Number of entries = number of baseline districts.
         mean_magnitude_baseline = mean(seats), # Total baseline seats divided by the district count.
         median_magnitude_baseline = median(seats), # Middle size; average the two middle values for an even district count.
         share_below9_pct_baseline = 100 * mean(seats < 9), # mean is the share with strictly fewer than 9 seats
         cv_magnitude_baseline = sqrt(mean((seats - mean(seats))^2)) / mean(seats)) # Population SD divided by mean
})
stopifnot(all(is.finite(eq1_baseline$cv_magnitude_baseline)),
          all(eq1_baseline$cv_magnitude_baseline >= 0)) # CV must be finite and nonnegative.

eq1_cantons <- eq1_elections |>
  group_by(canton) |> # Collapse election-level outcomes into one row per canton.
  summarise(
    elections = n(), districts_min = min(districts), districts_max = max(districts),
    mean_gain_pp = mean(seat_gain_pp), .groups = "drop" # Average outcomes across elections, giving each election equal weight.
  ) |>
  left_join(eq1_baseline, by = "canton") # Attach fixed historical predictors
stopifnot(!anyNA(eq1_cantons),
          all(eq1_cantons$districts_min == eq1_cantons$districts_max),
          all(eq1_cantons$baseline_districts == eq1_cantons$districts_min)) # Check no missing values and consistent district counts.

# The cutoff for each measure is the unweighted mean across transition cantons.
eq1_points <- eq1_cantons |>
  select(canton, mean_gain_pp, ends_with("_baseline")) |> # Keep the outcome and four baseline measures for plotting.
  pivot_longer(-c(canton, mean_gain_pp), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") |> # One row per canton and measure.
  group_by(metric) |> # Each measure has its own cutoff and groups.
  mutate(cutoff = mean(value[canton != "GR"]), # Unweighted mean of the eight transition cantons; exclude GR.
         group = case_when(canton == "GR" ~ "GR: context only",
                           value < cutoff ~ "Below mean",
                           TRUE ~ "At/above mean")) |> # GR gets a context label; equality with the cutoff goes in the upper group.
  ungroup() |> # Remove grouping before setting display labels.
  mutate(metric = factor(
    metric,
    levels = c("mean_magnitude_baseline", "median_magnitude_baseline",
               "share_below9_pct_baseline", "cv_magnitude_baseline"),
    labels = c("Mean district size (seats)", "Pre-reform median size (seats)",
               "Districts below 9 seats (%)", "Pre-reform district-size CV")),
    group = factor(group, c("Below mean", "At/above mean", "GR: context only"))) # Factors control panel and legend order.
eq1_groups <- eq1_points |>
  filter(canton != "GR") |> # Context canton does not contribute to group comparisons.
  group_by(metric, group) |> # Summarize each below-mean or upper group separately for each measure.
  summarise(cantons = n(), mean_gain_pp = mean(mean_gain_pp),
            members = paste(sort(canton), collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop") # Count cantons, average their gains equally, and list members.
eq1_differences <- eq1_groups |>
  select(metric, group, mean_gain_pp) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = mean_gain_pp) |> # Put the two group means in separate columns.
  mutate(below_minus_above_pp = `Below mean` - `At/above mean`) # Negative = the below-mean group gained less.
eq1_cutoffs <- eq1_points |>
  distinct(metric, cutoff) # One cutoff per measure, used in the text and dashed lines.

knitr::kable( # Render table
  eq1_cantons |>
    transmute(
      Canton = canton, Districts = baseline_districts,
      `Reference year` = reference_year,
      `Mean seats` = sprintf("%.2f", mean_magnitude_baseline), # Display two decimals; underlying values remain unrounded.
      `Pre-reform median` = sprintf("%.2f", median_magnitude_baseline),
      `Below 9 seats (%)` = sprintf("%.1f", share_below9_pct_baseline), # Display this percentage with one decimal.
      `Pre-reform CV` = sprintf("%.2f", cv_magnitude_baseline)
    ),
  align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r") # Left-align canton names; right-align the numerical columns.
)
```
*Notes* Source: author's calculations using official cantonal allocations and court judgments. To compute the measures for Uri, only the four DP consitutiencies (Municpialities) were taken.

@fig-district-magnitude relates each district measure to the canton-level mean gain in smaller parties' seat share. Colours distinguish cantons below and at or above the unweighted cross-canton mean of the respective measure. The cutoffs are defined by the mean of the eight relevant cantons and are the following: `r sprintf("%.2f", eq1_cutoffs$cutoff[eq1_cutoffs$metric == "Mean district size (seats)"])` seats for the unweighted mean magnitude, `r sprintf("%.2f", eq1_cutoffs$cutoff[eq1_cutoffs$metric == "Pre-reform median size (seats)"])` seats for median magnitude, `r sprintf("%.2f", eq1_cutoffs$cutoff[eq1_cutoffs$metric == "Districts below 9 seats (%)"])`% for the share below nine seats, and `r sprintf("%.2f", eq1_cutoffs$cutoff[eq1_cutoffs$metric == "Pre-reform district-size CV"])` for the CV. A CV of 0.6 means, that the standard deviation is 60% of the mean. The cross-canton means are marked with dashed lines.

```{r}
#| label: fig-district-magnitude
#| fig-cap: "Smaller-party seat-share gains by district magnitude and dispersion"
#| fig-width: 8.3
#| fig-height: 6.8
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

eq1_colours <- c("Below mean" = "#0072B2", "At/above mean" = "#D55E00",
                 "GR: context only" = "#8A8A8A") 
eq1_scatter <- ggplot(eq1_points, aes(value, mean_gain_pp, colour = group)) + # x = district measure; y = canton gain
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey70", linewidth = .35) + # Reference line where DP and HB give equal smaller-party shares.
  geom_vline(data = eq1_cutoffs, aes(xintercept = cutoff), inherit.aes = FALSE,
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60", linewidth = .4) + 
  geom_point(size = 2.8) + # One point per canton in each panel.
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = canton), seed = 1, size = 3.3,
                  max.overlaps = Inf, show.legend = FALSE) + # Repel canton labels
  facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free_x", ncol = 2) + # Four panels in two columns; separate x scales because units differ.
  scale_colour_manual(values = eq1_colours, drop = FALSE) + 
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(.12, .15))) + # Add space at the plot edges for labels.
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(.12, .15))) +
  labs(x = "District measure (fixed historical baseline)",
       y = "Mean smaller-party seat-share gain (pp)", colour = NULL, 
       caption = "Dashed lines: means across eight transition cantons. GR is contextual; Uri covers four DP municipalities.") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
        plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 8.5)) # Legend below, no minor grid, bold panel titles, left-aligned caption.
eq1_scatter # Print the saved plot into the thesis figure.
```

Figure 2, shows no clear, consistent relationship between the former district structure and the relative smaller parties seat gain across the eight relevant cantons. For the mean and median district magnitudes, it was expected that cantons with smaller districts would see larger gains for smaller parties. Instead is the analysis slightly pointing into the opposite direction, as also visible in the later discussed @fig-district-magnitude-groups. Moreover is no clear pattern visible when comparing the groups above and below the `r sprintf("%.2f", eq1_cutoffs$cutoff[eq1_cutoffs$metric == "Districts below 9 seats (%)"])`% share of districts with a maximum of eight seats. The observation of a missing clear correlation, is further the case in the analysis on the pre-reform district-size cv. Followingly in @fig-district-magnitude-groups , the same outcomes will be displayed as grouped dot plots with group means which makes the differences between the groups visually easier to assess. The missing paterns may be caused by the restricted amount of cantons and their different application of the Double Pukelsheim. 

```{r}
#| label: fig-district-magnitude-groups
#| fig-cap: "Smaller-party seat-share gains by historical district characteristics"
#| fig-width: 10.5
#| fig-height: 4.4
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

eq1_group_points <- filter(eq1_points, canton != "GR") # only include the 8 relevant transition cantons
eq1_group_means <- eq1_groups # Start with equally weighted group means 
eq1_size_membership <- eq1_group_points |>
  filter(metric %in% c("Mean district size (seats)", "Pre-reform median size (seats)")) |>
  select(canton, metric, group) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = metric, values_from = group) # Put each cantons results/measures together
eq1_combine_size <- all(eq1_size_membership[[2]] == eq1_size_membership[[3]]) # Check whether every canton has the same group in both
if (eq1_combine_size) { # Combine panels only when the group membership matches
  eq1_group_points <- eq1_group_points |>
    filter(metric != "Pre-reform median size (seats)") |> # Remove duplicate median grouping from plotted points
    mutate(metric = recode(as.character(metric),
                           `Mean district size (seats)` = "Baseline mean / median size"))
  eq1_group_means <- eq1_group_means |>
    filter(metric != "Pre-reform median size (seats)") |> # Remove duplicate group means
    mutate(metric = recode(as.character(metric),
                           `Mean district size (seats)` = "Baseline mean / median size"))
  eq1_group_levels <- c("Baseline mean / median size", "Districts below 9 seats (%)",
                        "Pre-reform district-size CV")
  eq1_group_points$metric <- factor(eq1_group_points$metric, eq1_group_levels)
  eq1_group_means$metric <- factor(eq1_group_means$metric, eq1_group_levels) # Keep points and means in the same panel order.
}
eq1_group_plot <- ggplot(eq1_group_points, aes(group, mean_gain_pp, colour = group)) + # x = below/above group; y = canton-average gain.
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey70", linewidth = .35) +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) + 
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = canton), seed = 1, size = 3.1,
                  nudge_x = .15, direction = "y", box.padding = .5,
                  max.overlaps = Inf, show.legend = FALSE) + # Move canton labels mainly vertically to improve readability.
  geom_point(data = eq1_group_means, shape = 18, size = 5, colour = "black") + # Add a black diamond for each group's mean gain.
  facet_wrap(~ metric, nrow = 1) + # Show the measure panels in a single row.
  scale_colour_manual(values = eq1_colours, drop = TRUE) + # Reuse blue/orange colours
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(.12, .15))) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean smaller-party seat-share gain (pp)", colour = NULL,
       caption = "Notes: canton averages. Black diamonds: equally weighted group means. GR excluded.") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "none", panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 14),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
        plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 14, lineheight = 1.1))
eq1_group_plot # Print the saved group-comparison plot into the thesis.
```

*Notes:* Cantons are grouped below or at or above the cross-canton mean of each historical district measure. 

For both mean district magnitude and pre-reform median district magnitude, the average gains for the below mean group are `r sprintf("%.2f", eq1_groups$mean_gain_pp[eq1_groups$metric == "Mean district size (seats)" & eq1_groups$group == "Below mean"])` and `r sprintf("%.2f", eq1_groups$mean_gain_pp[eq1_groups$metric == "Mean district size (seats)" & eq1_groups$group == "At/above mean"])` percentage points for the at/above mean group. The at/above group results, are relatively spread out, while the below groups cantons are quite close to eachother. The below-minus-above difference is `r sprintf("%+.2f", eq1_differences$below_minus_above_pp[eq1_differences$metric == "Mean district size (seats)"])` percentage points and with that opposite to the expected direction. 

For the share of districts below nine seats, the average gains for the below mean group are `r sprintf("%.2f", eq1_groups$mean_gain_pp[eq1_groups$metric == "Districts below 9 seats (%)" & eq1_groups$group == "Below mean"])` and `r sprintf("%.2f", eq1_groups$mean_gain_pp[eq1_groups$metric == "Districts below 9 seats (%)" & eq1_groups$group == "At/above mean"])` percentage points for the at/above mean group. The higher-share group gains of `r sprintf("%.2f", -eq1_differences$below_minus_above_pp[eq1_differences$metric == "Districts below 9 seats (%)"])` percentage points more are consistent with the expected direction. However is in the below group Schaffhausen included, whose comparatively high gain raises the group average. As discussed in @sec-h1-results does the separate treatment of affiliated lists contribute to Schaffhausen's high gain. Therefore the result needs to be interpreted sensitively. 

For pre-reform district-size variation, the average gains for the below mean group are `r sprintf("%.2f", eq1_groups$mean_gain_pp[eq1_groups$metric == "Pre-reform district-size CV" & eq1_groups$group == "Below mean"])` and `r sprintf("%.2f", eq1_groups$mean_gain_pp[eq1_groups$metric == "Pre-reform district-size CV" & eq1_groups$group == "At/above mean"])` percentage points for the at/above mean group.  The below-minus-above difference is  therefore `r sprintf("%+.2f", eq1_differences$below_minus_above_pp[eq1_differences$metric == "Pre-reform district-size CV"])` percentage points. This means that the group of cantons with the higher variation in district sizes relative to their mean in average had higher gains. Here, too Schaffhausen's relatively high gain raises the group average, leading to that the result should be interpreted sensitively.

To analyze the sensitivity of the results to certain cantons, a leave one canton out check was carried out. The check showed that the results in exploratory question 1 are sensitive to the omission of the canton of Schaffhausen. The omission of the canton of Schaffhausen, lets the mean and median measure decline from -3.06 to -1.06. For the share below 9 seats and the CV measure though the direction switches with the omission of the canton. This means that without the canton of Schaffhausen, the average gains for the below mean groups are higher than for the above mean group, which oposses the estimated direction. Generally is there substantial variation in both groups, which means that also the omission of cantons like Uri and Valais have substantial impact on some of the measures. The exact results to the robustness checks can be found in @sec-leave-one-out.

Taken together, the four district measures reveal no consistent pattern linking the initial district structure to smaller parties’ gains. This is combined with substantial variation within the analyzed groups. Further are the four measures sensitive to the omission of single cantons. Which supports the assesment of a missing pattern. The sensitivity to Schaffhausen can be linked to its comparatively high seat-share gain. Which is partly caused as discussed in @sec-data-cleaning by the separate classification of affiliated lists as smaller parties. These descriptive comparisons therefore can not show any causal effect of district magnitude or its dispersion.

#### Exploratory question 2: Differences by DP seat count (Parliament size)

The following expoloratory question examines possible differences of the smaller party seat share gain between the different amounts of seats distributed with DP and with the parliament size. As priorly mentioned is the variable *seats_allocated_dp* used since in the canton of Uri only four municipialities use the Double Pukelsheim system and with that only 37 of the parliaments 64 seats are distributed by the new system. The comparison below averages elections within each canton before comparing the two groups defined by the number of seats allocated through Double Pukelsheim. Graubünden is as always only shown for context and excluded from the group means.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-dp-seat-count
#| tbl-cap: "Mean smaller-party seat-share gain by number of seats allocated under Double Pukelsheim (Parliament size)"
#| echo: false

h1a_cantons <- small_party_summary |>
  mutate(canton = str_sub(election_id, 1L, 2L)) |> 
  group_by(canton) |>
  summarise(
    elections = n(),
    dp_seats = first(seats_allocated_dp),
    parliament_seats = first(parliament_size),
    mean_gain_pp = mean(seat_gain_pp),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
 mutate(
  size_group = case_when(
    canton == "GR" ~ "Context only (former Majorz)",
    dp_seats >= 100L ~ "At least 100 DP seats",
    TRUE ~ "Fewer than 100 DP seats"
  )
) |>
arrange(desc(dp_seats), canton)

h1a_groups <- h1a_cantons |>
  filter(canton != "GR") |>
  group_by(size_group) |>
  summarise(cantons = n(), mean_gain_pp = mean(mean_gain_pp), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable( 
  h1a_cantons |>
    transmute(Canton = canton, Group = size_group,
              Elections = elections,
              `DP seats (parliament)` = paste0(dp_seats, " (", parliament_seats, ")"),
              `Mean gain (pp)` = sprintf("%.1f", mean_gain_pp))
)
```

*Notes* Source: author's aggregation of the official cantonal election datasets.

The mean of the canton-level gains is `r sprintf("%.1f", h1a_groups$mean_gain_pp[h1a_groups$size_group == "At least 100 DP seats"])` percentage points in the group with atleast 100 Double Pukelsheim seats and `r sprintf("%.1f", h1a_groups$mean_gain_pp[h1a_groups$size_group == "Fewer than 100 DP seats"])` percentage points in the group with at most 100. The atleast-fewer difference is therefore `r sprintf("%+.1f", h1a_groups$mean_gain_pp[h1a_groups$size_group == "At least 100 DP seats"] - h1a_groups$mean_gain_pp[h1a_groups$size_group == "Fewer than 100 DP seats"])` percentage points.

To visualize the analysis of a possible relationship between parliament size and the smaller parties seat-share gain, is visualized in a scatterplot. In @fig-dp-seat-count each canton's average smaller-party-seat-share is plotted against the number of seats allocated through Double Pukelsheim. The two cantons are distinguished by colours, while Graubünden is displayed separately for context. 

```{r}
#| label: fig-dp-seat-count
#| fig-cap: "Smaller-party seat-share gains by Double Pukelsheim seat count"
#| fig-width: 8.3
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

ggplot(h1a_cantons, # reuse the table's dataset
       aes(x = dp_seats, y = mean_gain_pp, colour = size_group)) + # set y and x-axis
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey70", linewidth = .35) + 
  geom_vline(xintercept = 100, linetype = "dashed", # mark cutoff value
             colour = "grey60", linewidth = .4) +
  geom_point(size = 2.8) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(label = canton), seed = 1, size = 3.3, # label all cantons and reduce overlap
                  max.overlaps = Inf, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c( # set colors for groups
    "Fewer than 100 DP seats" = "#0072B2",
    "At least 100 DP seats" = "#D55E00",
    "Context only (former Majorz)" = "#8A8A8A"
  )) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(.12, .15))) + 
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(.12, .15))) +
  labs(
    x = "Seats allocated through Double Pukelsheim", # label the x-axis
    y = "Mean smaller-party seat-share gain (pp)", # label the y-axis
    colour = NULL,
    caption = "Dashed line: 100-seat cutoff. Uri covers four DP municipalities."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) + # apply the minimal theme
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 8.5)
  )
```

The @fig-dp-seat-count reveals no clear consistent relationship between DP seat count and smaller parties average seat share gains across the eight cantons in the main analysis. Which is also illustrated through the fact, that the mean of both groups is with 6.3, respectively 6.7 percentage points close together. Noticeable again is the high seat-gain share of Schaffhausen, which was priorly discussed for e.g. in @sec-h1-results. Since this comparison is based on only `r sum(h1a_groups$cantons)`  cantons operating under distinct electoral rules. Group averages may also conceal substantial variation between individual cantons, and the observed difference could reflect other institutional characteristics rather than the number of seats itself. The results therefore describe a difference within this sample but do not establish that a larger number of Double Pukelsheim seats causes greater gains.

#### Exploratory question 3: Explicit electoral quorums {#sec-eq3}

Exploratory question 3 researches on whether the implementation of explicit electoral quroums have an influence on the smaller parties seat-share gain. The explicit quroums ensure that only parties which reach a specific vote-share are considered for the allocation of seats. This may prevent smaller parties from entering the parliament, which is why it's expected in this thesis, that in cantons with a quorum, the seat-share gain of smaller parties is reduced. This directional estimation is analyzed followingly: 
```{=typst}
#[
#set table(
  stroke: 0.5pt,
  inset: 5pt,
)
```
| Canton | implemented Thresholds | relevant years |
|---|---|---|
| Aargau | none | 2009 |
| Aargau | 5% district level or 3% cantonal level | 2012, 2016, 2020, 2024 |
| Graubünden |3% cantonal level | 2022, 2026|
| Nidwalden | none | 2014, 2018, 2022, 2026 |
| Schaffhausen | none | 2008, 2012, 2016, 2020, 2024 |
| Schwyz | 1% cantonal level | 2016, 2020, 2024 |
| Uri | none | 2020, 2024 |
| Valais | 8% district level | 2017, 2021 ,2025  |
| Zug | 5% district level or 3% cantonal level | 2014, 2018, 2022, 2026 |
| Zurich | 5% district level | 2007, 2011, 2015, 2019 |
| Zurich | 5% district level or 3% cantonal level | 2023 |

: Situation regarding explicit electoral thresholds under Double Pukelsheim in the elections studied. {#tbl-explicit-quroums tbl-colwidths="[20, 45, 35]"}

Source: Author’s compilation. Threshold rules are based on the sources discussed in @sec-adoption. Election years refer to the elections included in the empirical analysis, whose data sources are documented in @sec-data-appendix.

```{=typst}
]
```
As documented in the table, out of eight analysis cantons, five applied a threshold. With Aargau being a special case, since the canton applied it only after their first election under Double Pukelsheim. The most often used explicit qourum is the combination of a 5% district-level and a 3% cantonal level threshold of which atleast one has to be reached. This combination was used in 9 of 19 elections held with an explicit threshold. 

The difference is visualized followingly, in a bivariate analyisis presented as a grouped dot plot.
```{r}
#| label: fig-quorums
#| fig-cap: "Smaller-party seat-share gains by explicit electoral quorum."
#| fig-height: 6
#| echo: false
eq3_elections <- small_party_summary |> 
  mutate( 
    canton = str_sub(election_id, 1, 2), # extract canton code from election ID
    quorum = case_when( 
      election_id == "AG_09" ~ "Without explicit quorum", # Aargau introduced its quorum for the 2012 election.
      canton %in% c("NW", "SH", "UR") ~ "Without explicit quorum", 
      canton %in% c("AG", "GR", "SZ", "VS", "ZG", "ZH") ~ "With explicit quorum",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    quorum = factor(
      quorum,
      levels = c("Without explicit quorum", "With explicit quorum")
    )
  )

stopifnot(!anyNA(eq3_elections$quorum)) # Check that all elections have been assigned a quorum category

eq3_cantons <- eq3_elections |> # Collapse election-level outcomes into one row per canton and quorum category.
  filter(canton != "GR") |>
  group_by(quorum) |>
  summarise(
    cantons = n_distinct(canton),
    elections = n(),
    mean_gain_pp = mean(seat_gain_pp),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

eq3_groups <- eq3_cantons |> # Summarize the mean gain for each quorum category.
  select(quorum, mean_gain_pp) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = quorum, values_from = mean_gain_pp) |>
  mutate(without_minus_with_pp = `Without explicit quorum` - `With explicit quorum`)

eq3_group_plot <- ggplot(eq3_elections, aes(quorum, seat_gain_pp, colour = quorum)) + # x = quorum category; y = canton-average gain.
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey70", linewidth = .35) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = if_else(canton == "GR", "context only", as.character(quorum))), size = 2.5) +
    geom_text_repel( # Place election labels around points with short connectors
    aes(label = election_id, colour = if_else(canton == "GR", "context only", as.character(quorum))), # label GR consistently with grey colour
    seed = 1,
    size = 3,
    nudge_x = .08,
    direction = "both",
    box.padding = .2,
    point.padding = .15,
    force_pull = 2,
    max.time = Inf, max.iter = 30000,
    segment.colour = "grey65", segment.size = .25,
    max.overlaps = Inf,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_point(data = eq3_cantons, aes(quorum, mean_gain_pp), shape = 18, size = 5, colour = "black") + # Add black diamond for group's mean gain.
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Without explicit quorum" = "#0072B2", "With explicit quorum" = "#D55E00", "context only" = "#8A8A8A")) + # colour the three categories
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Aggregate smaller-party seat-share gain (pp)", colour = NULL,
       caption = "Notes: individual elections Black diamonds: equally weighted group means") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "none", panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size = 12),
        plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 9)) 
eq3_group_plot # Print the saved group-comparison plot into the thesis.
```

@fig-quorums provides a descriptive comparison of smaller-party seat-share gains by the presence of an explicit electoral quorum. Average gains are higher in the group without an explicit quorum (`r sprintf("%.1f", eq3_cantons$mean_gain_pp[eq3_cantons$quorum == "Without explicit quorum"])` percentage points) than in the group with one (`r sprintf("%.1f", eq3_cantons$mean_gain_pp[eq3_cantons$quorum == "With explicit quorum"])` percentage points). Both groups exhibit substantial variation. From which the canton of Schaffhausen sticks out, as mentioned in prior analysises. 

To analyze whether the effect holds despite the variation, the leave one canton out sensitivity check was performed. As priorly is the high seat-share gain of Schaffhausen making the analysis and the results sensitive to the omission of it. Schaffhausen accounts for five of the twelve elections in the group without an explicit quorum, with all five recording seat-share gains above the group average. With Schaffhausen's exclusion is the difference flipping from 3.56 to -0.67. That means without Schaffhausen, the observed effect is not aligned anymore with the expectation, that in cantons without an explicit quorum the seat-share gain is higher. The exact results for the omission of every canton are outlined in @sec-leave-one-out.

Especially interesting, is the case of the canton Aargau, where in 2009 the election was held without a threshold and in the elections 2012, 2016, 2020 and 2024 with a threshold. The data shows that the seat-share gain for the pre-reform election 2009 and the first post-reform election 2012 is equally big with 9.3 percentage points. In the subsequent elections, though the seat-share gain droped accordingly to the assumption. While the unchanged gain between 2009 and 2012 contrasts with the assumption, the subsequent elections are inline with it. For Aargau there is therefore no clear pattern visible, moreover might the seat-share gain difference be influenced by further unobserved circumstances. 

To summarize the analysis about the effect of the implementation of explicit quoroms, it can be stated that within the 31 relevant election a difference which matches the expectaion can be seen. This difference though is sensitive to the inclusion of Schaffhausen. Further is the limited amount of elections held till date and the different application of thresholds and electoral law, encouraging to interpret the difference with caution.

#### Exploratory question 4: Change across successive elections

The preceding analysis showed that cantons differ in their implementation of the Double Pukelsheimer system. These institutional differences motivate a closer examination of within-canton patterns. The last exploratory question therefore examines how the smaller parties seat-share gain changed across successive elections within a canton. For that each canton and it's successive changes are analyzed separately. To possibly better understand changes, events such as electoral reforms and changes in the party composition are documented. Generally stable positive values of $\Delta_e$ indicate a persistent mechanical advantage for smaller parties, while substantial fluctuation or even changes in sign would suggest that the effect is strongly dependent on the individual circumstances of an election. 

Since @fig-successive-elections aligns every Double Pukelsheim election for each canton independently by their order, the first election under the system is numbered 1, the next is numbered 2, and so on. This means that the same election number represents different calendar years across cantons.  As in the main hypothesis the outcome is the observed Double Pukelsheim seat share minus the counterfactual Hagenbach-Bischoff seat share, expressed in percentage points of the seats included in the comparison. The smaller-party category is recalculated for each election using the existing vote-share cutoff of less than 10%.

Regarding the events and their noteboxes, there are two different formats. The bigger boxes mark electoral rule changes, from which there were three relevant ones: Aargau's introduction of a 5% district-level or 3% cantonwide quorum in 2012 (second election); Schaffhausen's majority clause, applied in 2016 (third election); and Zurich's additional 3% cantonwide eligibility route, first applied in 2023 (fifth election). The Zurich rule supplements the existing 5% district-level quroum and as in Aargau, the parties have to only reach either 5% within a district or 3% on the cantonal level. These dates follow the institutional history in @sec-adoption; Schaffhausen's amendment history records 1 March 2016 as the effective date of implementation (Kanton Schaffhausen, 1904/2019). The E/L annotations mark parliamentary parties entering or leaving the below-10% vote-share group; a preceding 2 indicates two parties. Graubünden is shown as priorly only contextual.

```{r}
#| label: fig-successive-elections
#| fig-cap: "Smaller-party seat-share gains across successive elections under Double Pukelsheim"
#| fig-width: 8.3
#| fig-height: 6.5
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

# Reuse the election-level outcome calculated for the main comparison.
# Number elections chronologically within each canton, rather than pooling years.
eq4_elections <- small_party_summary |>
  mutate(
    canton = str_sub(election_id, 1, 2),
    election_year = 2000L + as.integer(str_extract(election_id, "[0-9]{2}$")),
    net_seat_gain = seats_dp - seats_hb,
    comparison = if_else(is_graubuenden, "Context only", "HB transition")
  ) |>
  arrange(canton, election_year) |>
  group_by(canton) |>
  mutate(election_number = row_number()) |>
  ungroup()

stopifnot(
  !anyDuplicated(eq4_elections[c("canton", "election_year")]),
  !anyNA(eq4_elections$election_year),
  all(is.finite(eq4_elections$seat_gain_pp))
)


eq4_events <- tribble(
  ~canton, ~election_year, ~label, ~label_x,
  "AG", 2012L, "AG: quorum introduced", 1.55,
  "SH", 2016L, "SH: majority clause added", 3.15,
  "ZH", 2023L, "ZH: quorum changed", 4.75
) |>
  left_join(
    select(eq4_elections, canton, election_year, election_number, seat_gain_pp),
    by = c("canton", "election_year"),
    relationship = "one-to-one"
  )

# Smalle notes identify changes in membership of parliamentary parties in the below 10% group.
# E = one party enters below 10% Group, L = one party leaves below 10% Group , 2L = two parties ...
eq4_notes <- tribble(
  ~canton, ~election_year, ~label, ~label_x, ~label_y,
  "AG", 2020L, "L", 3.75, 2.15,
  "AG", 2024L, "E", 4.75, 6.0,
  "NW", 2026L, "E", 4.25, 13.65,
  "UR", 2024L, "E", 2.50, 0.70,
  "ZG", 2018L, "L", 1.50, 6.60,
  "ZH", 2011L, "L", 2.35, 15.00,
  "ZH", 2015L, "2E", 3.00, 16.40,
  "ZH", 2019L, "2L", 4.35, 8.70
) |>
  left_join(
    select(eq4_elections, canton, election_year, election_number, seat_gain_pp),
    by = c("canton", "election_year"),
    relationship = "one-to-one"
  )

# Fail explicitly if an event is accidentally mapped to an absent/wrong election.
stopifnot(
  !anyNA(eq4_events$election_number),
  identical(eq4_events$election_number, c(2L, 3L, 5L)),
  !anyNA(eq4_notes$election_number)
)

eq4_colours <- setNames(
  rep("#0e0000", 9),
  c("AG", "GR", "NW", "SH", "SZ", "UR", "VS", "ZG", "ZH")
)
eq4_canton_labels <- c(
  AG = "Aargau", GR = "Graubünden (context)", NW = "Nidwalden",
  SH = "Schaffhausen", SZ = "Schwyz", UR = "Uri",
  VS = "Valais", ZG = "Zug", ZH = "Zurich"
)

# Label each trajectory at its final available election.
# Offset the crowded endpoints while keeping their labels connected to the data.
eq4_line_labels <- eq4_elections |>
  group_by(canton) |>
  slice_max(election_number, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    label = if_else(canton == "GR", "Graubünden\n(context)",
                    unname(eq4_canton_labels[canton])),
    label_x = election_number + if_else(canton == "GR", -.15, .15),
    label_y = seat_gain_pp + case_when(
      canton == "GR" ~ 2, canton == "UR" ~ -2,
      TRUE ~ 0
    ),
    label_hjust = if_else(canton == "GR", 1, 0)
  )

# Reserve a band above the observed outcomes for the three arrow labels.
eq4_top <- max(eq4_elections$seat_gain_pp)
eq4_span <- max(1, diff(range(c(0, eq4_elections$seat_gain_pp))))
eq4_events <- eq4_events |>
  mutate(label_y = eq4_top + .30 * eq4_span)

eq4_plot <- ggplot(eq4_elections,
                   aes(election_number, seat_gain_pp, group = canton, colour = canton)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60", linewidth = .4) +
  geom_line(aes(linetype = comparison), linewidth = .8) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = canton), size = 2.6) +
  # Arrowheads end at the actual election outcome, not at its text label.
  geom_segment(
    data = eq4_events,
    aes(x = label_x, y = label_y,
        xend = election_number, yend = seat_gain_pp),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "grey55", linewidth = .3,
    arrow = grid::arrow(length = grid::unit(2, "mm"), type = "closed"),
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_label(
    data = eq4_events,
    aes(label_x, label_y, label = label, colour = canton),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 3.8, lineheight = 1.05,
    fill = "white", linewidth = .25,
    label.padding = grid::unit(.25, "lines"), show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = eq4_colours, breaks = names(eq4_colours),
                      labels = eq4_canton_labels) +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c(AG = 16, GR = 1, NW = 17, SH = 15, SZ = 18,
                                UR = 3, VS = 7, ZG = 0, ZH = 8),
                     breaks = names(eq4_colours), labels = eq4_canton_labels) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("HB transition" = "solid", "Context only" = "dashed"),
                        guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq_len(max(eq4_elections$election_number)),
    labels = function(x) paste0(x, ifelse(x == 1, "st", ifelse(x == 2, "nd", ifelse(x == 3, "rd", "th")))),
    limits = c(.6, 6.2), expand = expansion(mult = 0)
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = pretty(c(0, eq4_top)),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(.06, .10))) +
  labs(
    x = "Election under Double Pukelsheim (within each canton)",
    y = "Smaller-party net seat-share gain (pp)", colour = NULL, shape = NULL,
    caption = paste(
      "Gain = observed DP minus counterfactual HB; vote-share cutoff: below 10%.",
      "E / L: a parliamentary party enters / leaves the below-10% vote-share group.",
      "2E / 2L: two parliamentary parties enter / leave that group.",
      "Calendar years differ across cantons.",
      sep = "\n"
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(), panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 11),
    plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 11, lineheight = 1.1),
    plot.margin = margin(10, 12, 8, 8)
  )

eq4_plot <- eq4_plot +
  geom_segment(
    data = eq4_notes,
    aes(x = label_x, y = label_y,
        xend = election_number, yend = seat_gain_pp),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "grey55", linewidth = .25,
    arrow = grid::arrow(length = grid::unit(1.2, "mm"), type = "closed"),
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = eq4_notes,
    aes(x = label_x, y = label_y, label = label, colour = canton),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 3.2, lineheight = 1.05,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    data = filter(eq4_line_labels, label_y != seat_gain_pp),
    aes(x = election_number, y = seat_gain_pp,
        xend = label_x, yend = label_y),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "grey55", linewidth = .25,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = eq4_line_labels,
    aes(x = label_x, y = label_y, label = label,
        hjust = label_hjust, colour = canton),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, size = 3.4, lineheight = .95,
    show.legend = FALSE
  )
eq4_plot
```

*Notes* Sources: Large text boxes are based on the sources discussed in @sec-adoption. 
```{r}
#| label: eq4-summary
#| include: false

# Calculate average transition changes and average seat-share gain by election number
eq4_election_stats <- eq4_elections |>
  filter(!is_graubuenden) |> # Exclude Graubünden 
  arrange(canton, election_number) |> # Order elections chronologically for each canton
  group_by(canton) |> # Calculate changes separately for each canton.
  mutate(
    change_pp = seat_gain_pp - lag(seat_gain_pp) # calculate difference between preceeding and current election
  ) |>
  ungroup() |> # remove canton grouping for 2nd calculation
  group_by(election_number) |> # Group 1st, 2nd, 3rd etc elections together
  summarise(
    cantons = n_distinct(canton), # Count cantons for each group
    mean_gain_pp = mean(seat_gain_pp), # Calculate the equally weighted average seat-share gain.
    mean_change_pp = if (all(is.na(change_pp))) {
      NA_real_ # Election 0 doesn't exist, therefore excluded later in the note
    } else {
      mean(change_pp, na.rm = TRUE) # Average the within-canton changes, excluding missing values.
    },
    .groups = "drop" 
  ) |>
  arrange(election_number) # Display the results
```

::: {.callout-note title="EQ4 summary"} 
Excluding Graubünden, the average within-canton change in smaller parties’ seat-share gain was `r with(filter(eq4_election_stats, election_number > 1L), paste(sprintf("%+.1f percentage points from election %d to %d (%d cantons)", mean_change_pp, election_number - 1L, election_number, cantons), collapse = "; "))`. The average seat-share gains across the cantons were `r paste(sprintf("%.1f percentage points in election %d (%d cantons)", eq4_election_stats$mean_gain_pp, eq4_election_stats$election_number, eq4_election_stats$cantons), collapse = "; ")`. Each average gives equal weight to the cantons observed in both elections of the respective transition.
:::

Generally spoken, are the seat-share gains with some canton-specific fluctuations, relatively persistent. As seen in the analysis of Hypothesis 1, is with Uri 2020  only one election, in which there was no positive seat-share gain. This is the case, since there simply no *smaller_party* ran. Another interesting observation, is the fact that the average seat-share gain rises successively from election to election. This with the caveat of the limited number of cantons and that this number lowers throughout the later elections. For a possible effect speaking is, that the cantons of Schaffhausen and Zurich which appear in all comparisons and have relatively high seat-gain shares also experience drops in their share throughout the elections. This while the average seat-share gain rises continously. Additionally is the analysis, less dependent on political trends specific to a single election year, since for example the second elections held under Double Pukelsheim range from 2011 in Zurich to 2024 in Uri. This though does not isolate the pattern from political trends. A possible partial explanation for the observed pattern, is the broader increase in party-system fragmentation, which was documented by Lüscher (2024, pp. 133-135). This because if smaller parties receive wider support, their combined disadvantage under the former Hagenbach-Bischoff and with that their seat-share gain under Double Pukelsheim may increase. Nevertheless, whether this mechanism actually explains the observed pattern remains untested.

Besides the broader image, there are also interesting patterns within the cantons. The biggest changes between two elections, can be seen for Schaffhausen, Zurich and Nidwalden. In Schaffhausen the seat-share gain rose from the first to the 2nd election from roughly 10 to roughly 17 percentage points, where it settled afterward quite stable. A possible partial reason, is the higher number of smaller parties in the parliament which increased from seven in 2008 to nine in 2012. From the 2015 Zurich, to the 2019 Zurich election, the seat-share gain dropped by roughly 5 percentage points, a reason for this is possibly, that both the GLP and the Greens exceeded the 10% smaller-parties threshold while the BDP lost its parliamentary representation. This led to the circumstance, that from seven smaller parliamentary parties in 2015, the number dropped to four in 2019. In Nidwalden since the implementation the seat-gain share rose continously. The strongest difference  was observed from the 3rd to the 4th election, where the share rose by 5 percentage points. This effect might be partially influenced by the in the smaller party composition, since the green party fell below the 10% threshold.  For Aargau, Zug, Schwyz and Valais we can observe relatively stable patterns with smaller fluctuations. For the canton of Uri only two elections were observed, which is why no pattern can be inferred. 

In the three cantons Aargau, Schaffhausen and Zurich, the Double Pukelsheim system, was adjusted after its implementation. The case of the canton of Aargau was priorly discussed in @sec-eq3. The assumption of the implementation of a threshold is that the smaller-party seat share gain declines with it. The post electoral change results for the canton of Aargau don't present a clear picture there with results aswell in accordance as also speaking against the assumption. The absence of a clear effect, may be partly explained through that in each election the biggest list without parliamentary representation, received only between 0.1% to 0.7% vote shares.^[For cantonal vote shares and parliamentary representation, see T. Schaub (2012, p. 12), Staatskanzlei des Kantons Aargau (2016b, p. 2), Staatskanzlei des Kantons Aargau (2020, p. 2), and Staatskanzlei des Kantons Aargau (2024).] This suggests that the explicit quroums in Aargau only had limited scope to exclude parties, which otherwise would have won seats. In Schaffhausen in 2016 as described in @sec-adoption, a majority clause was implemented. This majority clause ensures that the strongest list in each constituency receives at least one seat. It does this, while preserving the seat allocation of the canton-wide upper apportionment. (Kanton Schaffhausen, 1904/2019, Art. 2d paras. 1bis and 2(b)) Thus it has no effect on the smaller party seat-share gain. In the canton of Zurich, in the year 2023 a quroum change applied. Since to the existing 5% district-level quroum a 3% canton-wide one was added, of which parties have to reach either one. This electoral change is in the tendency highering the seat-share gain, since it possibly enables more parties to reach the seat-allocation process. In the 2023 election, though no party profited from this clause, since every qualifying party also reached the 5% district-level threshold (Regierungsrat des Kantons Zürich, 2023, p.9). Further did the seat-share gain drop from the 2019 to the 2023 election. Overall did the three electoral changes therefore have no visible effect on the smaller party seat-share gain.

As for the other analyses, was here also a robustness check performed. The check was done for each election number separately. Throghout all checks does the seat-share gain remain positive. The mean change though from election three to four and from four to five switches signs when Zurich, respectively the canton of Aargau is excluded. These later transition include only five respectively three cantons and are therefore more sensitive to indidvidual cantons. The exact statistics for the robustness check can be found in @sec-leave-one-out.

The analyis across all 31 elections, therefore indicates that the mechanical seat-share gain for smaller parties persists across sucessive elections. The strength and variation in the magnitude differ between the cantons. In the analyzed elections, the gain not only persisted, but rose across sucessive elections. The average within-canton change though isn't rising consecutively with a small decline between the third and fourth election. Moreover is the analysis for the within-canton change sensitive to the canton of Zurich, respectively Aargau in the two last transitions. The analysis and it's effects may be partly affected through the changes in the party composition of the smaller parties group. The results therefore imply a consistent gain for smaller-parties across cantons and elections. However it can't be established and is not inferred or mentioned by the literature, that additional elections under Double Pukelsheim increase the gain.

## Discussion

In this paper, the general question: "20 Years of the Double Pukelsheim System in Switzerland: What Is the Mechanical Effect of the Transition from the Hagenbach-Bischoff Method on the Seat Distribution of Smaller Parties? " was answered in two parts. In the first step, the mechanical effect on the smaller parties was examined. Subsequently the study examined which conditions could lead to differences in the strength of the mechanical effect across cantons or elections.

## Appendix

### Appendix 1: Explanation Data Cleaning Process {#sec-data-appendix}

The table below identifies the election data and legal sources used in the canton-specific cleaning scripts and counterfactual Hagenbach–Bischoff allocation. It specifies source titles, election coverage, file types, and the purpose of publications used to reconstruct or validate the results, together with the relevant legal provisions. Clickable citations and source titles lead to online sources where available; unpublished material supplied by email is identified explicitly. Author–year and case citations correspond to entries in the bibliography.

#### Smaller parties' absolute seat counts {#sec-absolute-seats-appendix}

@fig-small-parties-absolute supplements the seat-share comparison used to assess Hypothesis 1 in @fig-small-parties-relative. It shows the absolute number of seats won collectively by parties below the 10% vote-share threshold under the observed Double Pukelsheim allocation and the counterfactual Hagenbach-Bischoff allocation. The grey line connects the two outcomes for each election, with each election labelled at its Double Pukelsheim point. Because the number of analyzed seats differs across elections, these absolute counts provide context for the magnitude of the gains, while Hypothesis 1 is assessed using the difference in seat shares.
